author: artificialanlys
text:
We've updated the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, replacing SWE-Bench Pro with Datacurve's DeepSWE benchmark - the swap lifts Codex with GPT-5.5 (xhigh) above Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (max), while the newly released Claude Fable 5 (max) in Claude Code debuts at the top

DeepSWE, built by @datacurve, writes its tasks from scratch rather than adapting them from public GitHub issues or pull requests, so no model has seen the solutions during training. That matters because SWE-Bench Pro, the benchmark it replaces in our Coding Agent Index, had grown gameable, with some models recovering the fix from the repository's commit history instead of solving the task.

The swap reorders the index: Codex with GPT-5.5 (xhigh) rises from 65 to 76, overtaking Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (max) at 73. Claude Code with Fable 5 (max), which enters directly on the refreshed index, leads at 77. SWE-Bench Pro had been flattering some combinations and penalizing others.

More below.

author: smtgpt
text:
I have a keen interest in Spacetech. In fact, I have even invested in a solid Spacetech startup here in India (Will share more on that another day). The global focus today is on SpaceX’s IPO.

The reported numbers are very interesting
-Expected IPO price: $135/share
-Raise: ~$75B at  ~$1.75T valuation
-Demand: 3.5 to 4x oversubscribed
-Retail access: Up to 30% retail allocation

While the scale is massive, what genuinely excites me isn't just the size of the IPO. It is how and where the price discovery is happening. 

For decades, IPO pricing was a closed-door game controlled by bankers and a few privileged institutions.
But thanks to crypto rails, @SpaceX-linked perpetual futures have been trading publicly, 24/7, since mid-May.

Look at the public data:
– SPCX futures trading around $173.5 this morning vs. the $135 IPO price 
– A ~29% premium discovered before the bell even rings – Over $3.2B in cumulative volume and ~$390M in open interest.  

An important note: These are synthetic perps, not actual SpaceX shares (meaning no ownership or voting rights). But they prove an important point. Crypto markets are creating a live, liquid, and democratic signal of what the market actually thinks an asset is worth.

And the track record is honest, not perfect: Airbnb's futures undershot the 2020 pop. Coinbase's overshot at peak mania in 2021. But just last month, these markets called the Cerebras opening price within ~1.3%. As liquidity deepens, the signal sharpens. (Image generated via Claude Fable 5. In the comments)

Yes, three data points is a small sample. But the direction is unmistakable. We are shifting to an era where price discovery happens continuously, in public, weeks in advance! Later today, we find out how accurate the crowd's math is this time on SpaceX. 

But one thing is crystal clear: Price discovery is finally becoming public infrastructure and it will only get better when more people start participating in these global markets.

text:
$AMD could reach $2 Trillion Market Cap FY2027 🧵
W/ $TSM to solve @OpenAI @AnthropicAI Tokenomic Crisis
Not Financial Advice! DYOR!

“As these agents do work, they spawn more CPU tasks... We certainly see the movement towards where in the past the CPU to GPU ratio was primarily just as a host node in like a 1:4 or 1:8 configuration, now changing and getting closer to a 1-to-1 configuration or even... you can even imagine if you get lots and lots of agents that you could have more CPUs than GPUs.”
— Dr. Lisa Su, AMD Chair and CEO

Dr. Lisa Su’s observation captures the seismic shift now driving the tokenomic crisis, the transition from GPU-centric training to CPU-intensive, always-on agentic AI. What was once a supporting role for CPUs has become a primary bottleneck, colliding with severe supply constraints and fueling unsustainable inference costs for enterprises. 

1. Primary Causes of the Tokenomic Crisis

A.Explosive Agentic AI Demand and Token Multiplication

Agentic workflows with multi-step reasoning, tool calling, orchestration, retries, and long-horizon autonomy  consume 5–100x more tokens per task than traditional prompting. Frontier models like Anthropic’s Fable 5 (premium pricing + verbose outputs) and OpenAI’s advanced variants amplify this effect. Projections show global token demand potentially rising ~24x by 2030, with enterprises reporting budgets exhausted in weeks rather than years.

Anthropic Fable 5 (Mythos-class): $10 / $50 per million input/output tokens explicitly ~2x their prior flagship (Opus 4.8 at $5/$25). It's positioned as a premium agentic/reasoning model. This is unsustainable, hence we are seeing companies crying about Tokens bills.

OpenAI GPT-5.5 (current flagship): $5 / $30 per million, more affordable on a direct sticker-price basis than Fable 5. They also offer cheaper tiers like GPT-5.4 ($2.50/$15) and mini/nano variants for cost-sensitive work

B. CPU Supply Crunch as the Hidden Bottleneck

Traditional AI favored GPU-heavy ratios (1 CPU : 4–8 GPUs). Agentic systems reverse this dynamic to 1-5 CPU to 1 GPU,where CPUs manage orchestration, data loading, state management, external calls, and parallel task spawning, often leaving expensive GPUs idle while waiting on the host. The industry is rapidly shifting toward higher CPU ratios (or AMD new Agentic AI Rack). Server CPUs from AMD (EPYC) and Intel are largely sold out for 2026, with lead times stretching weeks to months and prices rising 10–35% in tight markets. TSMC’s heavy focus on AI accelerators has further squeezed CPU wafer capacity, raising overall cluster costs that flow directly into higher token pricing. Luckily, EPYC Venice has arrived and currently in mass production. 

C. Power, Networking, and Systemic Inefficiencies

Poor utilization, high power draw, and legacy networking overhead compound the problem. Hyperscalers and enterprises now demand balanced, power-efficient rack-scale solutions to scale sustainably without exploding operational expenses.

Surging consumption meets hardware scarcity 
→ elevated marginal costs 
→ provider pricing pressure and enterprise ROI scrutiny.

2. Why Increased TSMC 2nm Allocation for AMD Will Significantly Ease Token Costs

AMD has secured strong early access to TSMC’s 2nm (N2) process and significant allocation, positioning EPYC Venice as one of the first major HPC products to ramp on it, with production already advancing in Taiwan and Arizona. This allocation advantage delivers immediate relief on supply, performance, and efficiency. Bringing token cost at GW Scale to as low as $0.0003-$0.0005/M Tokens. TSMC is ramping up 2nm Fabs at the faster pace than prior 3nm expansion, up to 12 2nm/1.4nm Fabs by 2027/2028 to service $AMD Agentic AI demand.

~Core Density & Performance Up to 256 Zen 6 cores per socket, substantial compute uplifts, and higher memory bandwidth  directly alleviating the orchestration bottleneck in agentic workloads.
~2nm GAA transistors provide major improvements in performance-per-watt, critical for power constrained data centers and lower energy-per-token economics.
~Accelerated volume ramp (with Verano as the follow-on) will ease the 2026–2027 crunch, allowing hyperscalers like OpenAI and Meta to deploy more balanced clusters faster than allocation-constrained competitors.

3. The AMD Agentic AI Rack and Helios: Purpose-Built for the Agentic Era

AMD is addressing the exact gap Dr. Su highlighted with dense EPYC Venice “Agentic AI Racks”,  high-core-count CPU-optimized racks positioned between traditional servers and full GPU racks. These deliver massive orchestration capacity for fleets of agents.

~Optimized CPU:GPU Balance, Designed for 1:1 to 3–5:1 ratios that eliminate idle time and maximize end-to-end throughput.
~Rack-Scale Density,  Current EPYC Turin racks already exceed 27,000 cores; Venice pushes beyond 36,000 cores per rack, delivering up to 3.30x rack-level throughput versus NVIDIA Vera baselines in agentic workloads.
~Efficiency Gains, Lower power per token through superior density, liquid cooling compatibility, and system-level optimizations. Projections show potential inference costs dropping to $0.0001–$0.0005 per million tokens (or even lower with Verano).

H2 2026–2027: Venice-powered Agentic AI Racks and initial Helios deployments (already secured with major hyperscalers) relieve CPU constraints and lower underlying infrastructure costs, supporting token price relief. Pretty much CPUs are sold out for the next 3-5 years. 

Conclusion:

While much of the industry chased raw training FLOPs and GPU scarcity narratives, Dr. Lisa Su positioned AMD early and decisively around inference nearly 4 years ago, the real long-term driver of token economics. She recognized that agentic AI would fundamentally invert workloads, making efficient, abundant CPUs the key to sustainable scaling rather than GPU-only supremacy. 

By doubling down on high-core-density EPYC platforms, rack-scale systems like Helios and dedicated Agentic AI racks, and securing leading TSMC 2nm allocation, AMD is not merely reacting to the tokenomic crisis, it is actively solving it. This strategic clarity enables hyperscalers and enterprises to deploy balanced, power-efficient infrastructure that drives down real $/token costs, improves utilization, and restores economic viability to large-scale agentic deployments.

As Dr. Su anticipated the problem years in advance, AMD’s execution is now delivering the antidote. The result will be lower token prices, broader AI adoption, and a more balanced ecosystem where CPUs reclaim their central role AKA the brain. In the agentic era, the companies that solve the orchestration and efficiency bottlenecks, not just the matrix multiplications will define the winners. AMD, under Dr. Su’s leadership, is well-placed to be biggest TSMC customer in term of wafer as early as 2028.

quotedTweet.text:
Bon.

Première vraie journée sous Fable 5.

Et honnêtement, le résultat le plus surprenant n'est pas celui auquel je m'attendais.

Après plusieurs benchmarks (code, raisonnement business, workflows multi-agents), ma conclusion provisoire est que le vrai saut générationnel n'est pas Fable 5.

C'est Opus 4.7 → Opus 4.8.

Je pense que beaucoup de gens sous-estiment à quel point 4.8 est devenu bon.

Sur certaines tâches benchmarkées, Fable 5, Opus 4.8 et même parfois 4.7 finissent par produire le même résultat final.

La différence n'est plus vraiment :

"est-ce que le modèle sait résoudre le problème ?"

Mais plutôt :

combien de tours il lui faut
combien de tokens il brûle
combien il coûte
comment il arbitre dans l'incertitude
ce qu'il fait quand la tâche devient ambiguë

Autre constat intéressant :

Les systèmes multi-agents deviennent beaucoup plus difficiles à justifier qu'il y a 12 mois.

Quand les modèles étaient moins bons, l'orchestration augmentait directement la qualité.

Aujourd'hui, sur les tâches fermées et bien spécifiées, ce n'est plus forcément vrai.

Du coup je pense qu'une partie de l'industrie benchmark le mauvais problème.

Résoudre UNE tâche n'est plus très intéressant.

La vraie question devient :

Que se passe-t-il quand on donne 50 tâches simultanément à un système pendant plusieurs jours ?

Mémoire.
Coordination.
Arbitrage.
Priorisation.
Gestion du chaos.
C'est probablement là que se jouera la prochaine bataille.
Demain on passe à l'étape suivante :
50 tâches simultanées
40 événements injectés

plusieurs jours simulés

Claude seul vs Orchestria

Opus 4.8 vs Fable 5
Budget open bar. 😅

J'ai le sentiment qu'on va apprendre beaucoup plus sur l'avenir des agents avec ce benchmark qu'avec les 500 benchmarks de code habituels.

author: lagerskoy
text:
CLAUDE FABLE 5 IS PLAYING A DIFFERENT GAME

Same prompts, same tasks, same rules, yet the outputs don't even feel like they came from the same generation of AI. While other models produced decent simulations, Claude Fable 5 generated scenes that look closer to finished products than experiments. The fluid simulation has more depth, the lunar environment feels like an actual game world, and the black hole render looks like something pulled from a modern visualization engine rather than a chatbot response.

What's interesting isn't that one model won a benchmark. It's that the gap is becoming visible without charts, scores, or leaderboards. You can see it instantly. When people can identify the stronger model from a few seconds of video, the conversation shifts from "which AI is best" to "how far ahead is it"

The most dangerous thing about AI progress is that it happens gradually, then all at once. This video feels a lot like one of those moments.

text:
A 152 NODE FABLE 5 LATTICE FIRED 552 EDGES IN ONE PROMPT. THE SAME WORKFLOW UNDERCUTS $8,000 GAMING STUDIOS FOR $20

gamification agencies sell custom browser mini-games to brands at $3,000 to $8,000 per project. marketing teams buy them because an interactive thing holds attention longer than any banner

one builder typed a prompt chain into fable 5 and got back a gta-style open world game. driving, shooting, gang ai, cop chases, radar minimap. one html file, no engine, no assets

the trick is one feature per message. skeleton first, then on-foot mode, then combat, then polish. every step stays playable and nothing breaks under the previous layer

shipping takes a minute. drag the html file onto netlify drop, get a public link. no backend, no database, three.js loads from a cdn for free

the real product is the proof. a working interactive demo lands a client at $500 to $2,500 per reskin and agencies that quote $8,000 cannot move that fast

How to actually use Claude Fable, without burning your tokens.🔥

If you are blindly running Claude Fable 5 or specialized loop frameworks for your daily engineering tasks, you are setting yourself up for an astronomical API bill. 📉💰

Fable 5 is an absolute 10-trillion-parameter beast. But at $10 per million input tokens and a staggering $50 per million output tokens, letting it handle standard, low-leverage execution tasks is pure capital liquidation. 

To maximize frontier intelligence without hitting hard platform usage limits or draining your company's compute budget, you need a strict architectural strategy. 

Enter the **10/80/10 Hybrid System**. 

Here is how elite engineers are routing their workflows to extract 100% of Fable’s power at a fraction of the cost:

🏗️ The 10%: The Architect Phase (Fable 5)
Never use Fable 5 to write routine code or generic text blocks from scratch. Instead, use it exclusively at the very beginning of a project as your **Master Systems Architect**. 
• What to do: Feed Fable 5 your macro project goals, repository structures, and technical requirements. 
• The Output: Force the model to output a hyper-detailed, step-by-step structural blueprint, precise system specifications (`spec.md`), and modular prompt instructions for a lower-tier worker. You are paying the $50/M output fee only for high-leverage strategic planning.

⚙️ The 80%: The Worker Phase (Sonnet / Haiku / Local Models)
Once the master blueprint is compiled, swap out Fable entirely. You pass the `spec.md` and the modular sub-task scripts to highly efficient, cost-effective mid-tier models like Claude Sonnet or Haiku.
• What to do: Let the fast, cheap models handle the heavy lifting—writing the actual lines of code, parsing standard data blocks, formatting files, and compiling scripts based on Fable's rigid blueprint constraints. They do 80% of the mechanical, routine labor for a tiny fraction of the API cost.

🔍 The 10%: The Critic Phase (Fable 5)
Once the worker models have generated the code or assets, you bring Fable 5 back into the loop for the final mile. It acts as your **Master Quality Critic & Security Red-Teamer**.
• What to do: Feed the generated assets back to Fable 5. Have it scan the code for subtle logic gaps, hidden security vulnerabilities, or architectural deviations from the original `spec.md`. It reviews, approves, and polishes the final 10% before deployment.

🛠️ Official Guardrails for `/loop` and `/goal` Commands
When utilizing advanced terminal utilities like Claude Code, the native background loops can run completely wild, spinning up dozens of multi-agent turns that burn through your token tier limits in minutes. Implement these operational safety guardrails:
1️⃣ Set Hard Effort Dials: Always initialize Fable on the *lowest possible thinking effort setting*. Only dial up the cognitive compute when a lower-tier worker completely fails an execution check.
2️⃣ Bound the Budget: Never execute an open-ended loop command (like `sloop keep building until complete`) without a hard operational circuit breaker. Force the system to halt after a maximum of 3 to 5 multi-agent turns for human inspection.

The Takeaway:
Model routing and multi-tier engineering are no longer optional. The game isn't about using the "best" model for everything—it’s about knowing how to orchestrate a hierarchy of models. By using Fable 5 strictly as the Architect and the Critic, while forcing mid-tier engines to act as the raw labor, you get production-grade frontier outputs without the enterprise-level token hangover. 🖥️🛡️

author: d_vuln
text:
This week our founder and CEO @theonejvo spoke with @notLeonardCohen  at @ACSnewsfeed's Information Age about @AnthropicAI's release of Claude Fable 5, the most capable model the company has made publicly available to date.

The question hanging over the launch: do the safety guardrails actually hold under pressure?

Within hours of release, Jamieson ran Fable 5 through PolyRange, his contamination-resistant offensive-security harness where every target is a freshly generated web app the model has never seen. 

The finding was clear. On real, multi-step, authorised exploitation work, Fable 5 hands every turn over to Claude Opus 4.8 rather than doing the task itself, exactly as Anthropic said it would. Across a full agentic run, 181 of 181 served turns came back from Opus 4.8.

What makes this interesting is the bar it clears. The day-one cyber safeguard held under sustained, multi-turn agentic pressure, which is the harder case beyond the single-turn "plan a cyberattack" prompts most tests rely on.

Jamieson was careful to stress this was an early directional signal rather than a peer-reviewed finding, and he said plainly there may well be bypasses he had yet to probe.

That caveat proved timely, as, in the days since, Pliny the Liberator from BT6 publicly claimed a Fable 5 jailbreak using a multi-agent decomposition strategy. 

Full technical details are still being analysed, and early reporting suggests the picture is more nuanced than the headlines, but given his track record across essentially every major model, it raises a genuine question over whether the safeguard holds in every case. That remains to be confirmed. 

Which is rather the point, that is, a controlled verification on day one is a starting point for scrutiny, and the wider community pressure-testing these claims is how the real picture sharpens. 

Verifying a safety claim and trying to defeat one are both part of the same healthy process.

Grateful to Leonard and the ACS team for the thoughtful coverage.

author: oax_foundation
text:
Hey #OAX fam!

This week, Anthropic launched #Claude #Fable 5, the first version of its #Mythos-class model that anyone can access. 🤖 Until now, Mythos was locked to a small circle of approved orgs managing critical infrastructure across 15 countries.

Here's why this release is worth paying attention to 👇

🧠 Big capability, hard guardrails. 

Fable 5 reportedly shines at software engineering, knowledge work, and vision. But in high-risk areas - cybersecurity, biology, chemistry - it blocks responses and falls back to Claude Opus 4.8. Anthropic says this is rare though: ~95% of sessions run fully on Fable.

💰 Premium pricing. 

$10 per million input tokens, $50 per million output, this is double the cost of Opus 4.8. And this lands right as enterprises everywhere are side-eyeing their AI bills.

🔒 A new data-retention precedent. 

All Fable 5 and Mythos 5 traffic comes with mandatory 30-day retention - even for enterprises that previously had zero-retention agreements. #Anthropic says it won't train on the data, only use it to defend against novel attacks and jailbreaks. Whether other labs follow this playbook is one of the bigger questions here 🤔

📅 Staged rollout. 

Fable 5 is included in Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans through June 22 - after that, it switches to usage credits, with subscription access returning later.

The bigger picture: this launch comes just days after Anthropic publicly called for frontier labs to coordinate a "brake pedal" on AI development, and as the company gears up for the public markets. 

Shipping your most powerful model while warning about where the tech is headed? That tension is quickly becoming the defining dynamic in AI right now. 😅

For teams across #Asia evaluating frontier models, the question has shifted from "what can it do?" to "what conditions come with it?" 

Full story via TechCrunch: https://t.co/x1IoeIlJui

#grok #chatgpt #tech #innovation #claudeai

author: indutripat82427
text:
FABLE 5 ONE-SHOT A CALL OF DUTY ZOMBIES CLONE FROM A SINGLE LAZY PROMPT

No planning mode.

No back-and-forth.

No hours of prompting Claude.

Just one sentence:

"Make me a COD Zombies clone, single-player, and make the shooting feel good."

And Fable 5 shipped a playable game.

What came back:

a fully playable FPS in the browser
surprisingly satisfying movement and gunplay
most features worked on the first try
built entirely with Three.js
no game engine
no assets
no elaborate spec document

A few months ago, building something like this meant days of work.

Now it's a one-line prompt.

The distance between "I have an idea" and "I'm playing it" is collapsing fast.

We're entering an era where vibe-coding an entire game is becoming a one-sentence problem.

author: paulsolt
text:
Fable 5 redesigned my onboarding experience. 

- 30 minutes of planning
- 2 hours to MVP
- ~2 additional hours of polish

The new experience is feeling really, really good and the model felt like the best Anthropic model I have worked with to date.

It wasn't perfect though. Even with 30 minutes of planning in Plan mode, it still made mistakes. Don't expect the code or feature to be fully baked in one or two prompts.

- Settings UI clipped
- It misunderstood 2 features requests and implemented things wrong
- It was creative with the UI design, but still not polished
- I went back and forth about 25 times
- It's slow for interactive development

I burned through ~20% of my Weekly usage and my entire 5 hour usage window.

I do think it's worth a shot, but it feels pricey compared to GPT-5.5, which feels unlimited to me.

We'll see tomorrow how GPT-5.5 performs with the same task ... and I guess ~4 hours of effort.

Is Fable 5 that much better at UI? I still had UI bugs, which you can see in the images attached. Getting the padding to look decent too several prompts.

text:
Microsoft has reportedly restricted employee access to Anthropic's new Claude Fable 5 model over concerns linked to its data retention policy. 

Unlike other Claude models that run under Zero Data Retention, Fable 5 is part of Anthropic's Mythos-class models, which require prompts and outputs to be stored for 30 days for safety checks. 

The move has created an unusual split, as Microsoft customers can access the model through GitHub Copilot and Foundry, while Microsoft's own staff face internal restrictions until legal teams complete their review.

author: r3birth
text:
The story: this started as a few hours of ideation with just the chatbot. Prototype, playtest, tear it down, rebuild. Once the feel was close, I ported it to my Mac mini for a proper local build.

Fable 5 wrote the handoff package. A full game design doc, a tech spec with an 11-phase build plan, and an instruction file telling Claude Code exactly how to work.

Then I let Claude Code build it. A few hours in, I discovered it had been running on Sonnet the whole time (doh!). So I rebuilt everything with Fable 5. All 11 phases in about an hour and a half.

This was the first playtest. Long way to go, but I'm really happy with the start.

Nature’s call for researchers to share their experiences with the newly released Claude Fable 5 as a timely and important contribution to the ongoing conversation around frontier AI in science. Following the model’s broad public availability—set against Mythos 5’s more restricted initial access for trusted partners with planned expansion into biomedical research—we observe that safety guardrails continue to constrain meaningful engagement with biological and chemical content, precisely the domains where structured, methodology-driven agentic workflows could deliver the greatest value in areas such as transcriptomics, biomarker discovery, evidence synthesis, and protocol design.
This situation reinforces our conviction that the most impactful AI systems for medical research are those that combine high capability with reliable, reusable scientific processes and appropriately calibrated safeguards—enabling specialized agents to sustain complex, connected workflows rather than being limited by overly restrictive guardrails that inadvertently hinder legitimate scientific inquiry.

· 今日 X 上的 AI 舆情小结

今天 X 平台上有关 AI 的讨论主线是，AI 能力正从代码生成向全流程自动化运维拓展，同时伴随便利性升级和商业化、文化认同的激烈碰撞。共识主要体现在开发者对更灵活的 API 速率配额管理、AI 编码助手的能力提升以及自动化仓库维护降本增效的前景普遍持欢迎态度，并认可特斯拉 Full Self-Driving 在乘坐体验上的快速迭代。分歧则围绕这些更新展开，不少用户质疑 Codex “储蓄重置”能否真正解决高强度限流的痛点，Claude Code 与 Cursor、Copilot 的编码能力孰优孰劣尚无定论，开源仓库维护 agent 的安全性、可靠性以及 AI 上市公司的正式着装究竟是背离创新精神还是走向成熟，都引发了针锋相对的观点。潜在风险在于，AI 自主代码修改可能带来安全责任归属模糊与治理冲突，模糊的定价策略和商业分层可能侵蚀开发者信任，而自动驾驶仍面对安全性怀疑和文化转型若过于剧烈也可能削弱行业的创新活力。

🔹 💡 大佬观点(Influencer Insights)

📢 AI 行业日报：端侧模型爆发与 Agent 工程化深水区

🔹 一、今日核心热点：三大技术趋势

▫️ 1. **端侧模型（On-device Model）进入实用临界点**

多位博主密集验证端侧模型的生产力价值，标志着该领域从"技术演示"迈向"日常可用"：

• @zhixianio 展开"苦行僧式修行"：使用 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-oQ6-fp16-mtp 模型，通过 oMLX 运行 Native MTP，在 PA（OpenClaw）和 Coding 场景下，响应速度超越远程 LLM，且"智商在线，还能帮我多想多做一步"。他甚至用 Mac 跑端侧模型来"解冻饭团"——看似玩笑，实则验证端侧推理的实时性已可支撑物理世界交互。

• Google Gemma 4 系列成为焦点：@zhixianio 密集测试 Gemma 4 的 QAT（量化感知训练）版本、12B 多模态模型，评价其"日文邮件解析分类入库"性能不错，但指出中文音频识别"驴唇不对马嘴"、英文和日语表现优异。他特别提到 QAT 是"新的端侧模型优化思路"——训练阶段即假设会被量化，以此提升后续量化效果。

• 端侧 TTS 应用落地：@zhixianio 的播客《认知有县》E5 引入 Owlia（端侧 TTS）作为主持人，本身就是端侧模型的应用案例。

> 洞察：端侧模型的竞争已从"能不能跑"转向"跑得好不好、省不省、快不快"。Google 的 QAT、Apple 的 MLX 生态、阿里的 Qwen 系列正在形成三足鼎立。

▫️ 2. **Claude Fable 5：能力跃升与成本焦虑并存**

Anthropic 的 Fable 5 成为今日最具争议性的产品，呈现"技术惊艳"与"经济不可持续"的张力：

| 维度 | 观察 |
|------|------|
| 能力边界 | @zhixianio：40 分钟完成 70% 工作，还指出设计不合理之处；@dotey：Fable 5 完成复杂功能（导入 Figma 本地文件、重建设计系统），"没有 Fable 5 帮忙搞不定" |
| 时间/成本 | @Pluvio9yte：速度"像乌龟慢爬"，消耗为 Opus 的 1.5x；@dotey 引用案例：团队成员 10 小时消耗等值 $1,500；@vista8：Fable 5 思考 15 分钟才开始行动 |
| 使用策略 | @Pluvio9yte 建议开 `/effort max` 强度；@dotey 则因 Token 消耗"不敢随便选 Max" |

> 关键分歧：@Pluvio9yte 认为 Fable 5 是"Opus4.6++与 GPT-5.5++的结合版"，未到"非常惊艳"；而 @zhixianio 直呼"Shut up and take my money"。这种分歧反映了用户场景差异——前端 Demo 类任务 vs. 复杂工程化任务。

▫️ 3. **Agent 工程化：从 Vibe Coding 到 Contract First**

行业对 AI 编程的认知正在深化，从"炫技"进入"工程纪律"阶段：

• @Pluvio9yte 提出 "Contract First" 最佳实践："没有定义好契约，其他一切都是空谈"。他基于 OpenSpec 二开形成开发框架，将"全栈开发中容易漂移的上下文外化成契约，让人和 AI 都有稳定参照物"。

• @dotey 系统总结 Claude Design 经验：强调 Design System 防"AI 味"、Markup 局部修改、CLAUDE.md 上下文管理、单向同步流程（Design → Code）。

• @vista8 开发 "乔木 Goal Meta Skill" 和 "乔木 AI PRD Skill"，将"一句话需求"转化为 AI 可执行的 Goal 指令和 PRD 文档，解决"人喜欢的 PRD 和 AI 喜欢的不一样"的问题。

> 趋势判断：Agent 编程正在形成新的工程范式——不是取代软件工程，而是放大软件工程的重要性（@dotey 引用观点）。

🔹 二、独特观点与行业前瞻

▫️ 1. **机器人"GPT-3 时刻"：因果世界模型 vs. VLA**

@AI_Jasonyu 转述黄碧薇（@huang_biwei）与极客公园的对谈，提出激进预测："明年初（2027），机器人就会有 GPT-3 时刻"。

核心论点：
• 现有 VLA + 堆数据路径"根本不通"——桌面高 2 厘米机器人就 fail
• 因果大模型将 scaling 斜率从 0.2 拉到 0.8，"几百个 demo 顶别人一万个"
• 世界模型三阶：渲染（Sora）→ 模拟（李飞飞）→ 想象（因果大模型）
• 关键改写："压缩即智能" → "结构化的压缩才是智能"

> 前瞻意义：若此路径成立，机器人将从"模仿学习"跃迁至"因果推理"，物理世界泛化能力质变。

▫️ 2. **DeepSeek 招聘"Agent Harness 研究员"：新工种诞生**

@dotey 披露 DeepSeek 招聘 Agent Harness 研究员，定义 "Model + Harness = Agent"。

Harness 范畴包括：上下文管理、长期记忆、Subagent/Multi-Agent、自进化 Agent、模型与 Harness 共同进化等。这是业界首次系统性定义"Harness"作为独立研究领域，暗示 Agent 的竞争已从"模型能力"转向"工程封装能力"。

▫️ 3. **Token 经济学的悖论**

• @ruanyf 计算：OpenClaw 创始人月消耗 6030 亿 Token，等值 $130 万（员工免费使用），"如果放开使用，AI 编程比真人程序员昂贵多了"
• @lijigang 提出矫正："Token 消耗量是虚假指标，问题是否被更好解决才是真实指标"
• @dotey 观察到："越来越多的企业终于发现 AI 比员工还贵了"

> 深层矛盾：AI 编程的边际成本递减假设正在被颠覆——顶级模型的"智能密度"提升速度，赶不上 Token 价格的下降速度。

▫️ 4. **AI 对软件外包行业的冲击**

@dotey 引用 OpenDoor 案例：裁掉印度 200 多人离岸团队，以美国本土更小规模的 AI 原生团队取代。这是首个公开确认的"AI 替代外包"大规模案例，预示全球软件外包产业的重构。

· 今日 X 上的 AI 舆情小结

今天 X 平台上有关 AI 的讨论主线是，AI 能力正从代码生成向全流程自动化运维拓展，同时伴随便利性升级和商业化、文化认同的激烈碰撞。共识主要体现在开发者对更灵活的 API 速率配额管理、AI 编码助手的能力提升以及自动化仓库维护降本增效的前景普遍持欢迎态度，并认可特斯拉 Full Self-Driving 在乘坐体验上的快速迭代。分歧则围绕这些更新展开，不少用户质疑 Codex “储蓄重置”能否真正解决高强度限流的痛点，Claude Code 与 Cursor、Copilot 的编码能力孰优孰劣尚无定论，开源仓库维护 agent 的安全性、可靠性以及 AI 上市公司的正式着装究竟是背离创新精神还是走向成熟，都引发了针锋相对的观点。潜在风险在于，AI 自主代码修改可能带来安全责任归属模糊与治理冲突，模糊的定价策略和商业分层可能侵蚀开发者信任，而自动驾驶仍面对安全性怀疑和文化转型若过于剧烈也可能削弱行业的创新活力。

🔹 💡 大佬观点(Influencer Insights)

📢 AI 行业日报：端侧模型爆发与 Agent 工程化深水区

🔹 一、今日核心热点：三大技术趋势

▫️ 1. **端侧模型（On-device Model）进入实用临界点**

多位博主密集验证端侧模型的生产力价值，标志着该领域从"技术演示"迈向"日常可用"：

• @zhixianio 展开"苦行僧式修行"：使用 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-oQ6-fp16-mtp 模型，通过 oMLX 运行 Native MTP，在 PA（OpenClaw）和 Coding 场景下，响应速度超越远程 LLM，且"智商在线，还能帮我多想多做一步"。他甚至用 Mac 跑端侧模型来"解冻饭团"——看似玩笑，实则验证端侧推理的实时性已可支撑物理世界交互。

• Google Gemma 4 系列成为焦点：@zhixianio 密集测试 Gemma 4 的 QAT（量化感知训练）版本、12B 多模态模型，评价其"日文邮件解析分类入库"性能不错，但指出中文音频识别"驴唇不对马嘴"、英文和日语表现优异。他特别提到 QAT 是"新的端侧模型优化思路"——训练阶段即假设会被量化，以此提升后续量化效果。

• 端侧 TTS 应用落地：@zhixianio 的播客《认知有县》E5 引入 Owlia（端侧 TTS）作为主持人，本身就是端侧模型的应用案例。

> 洞察：端侧模型的竞争已从"能不能跑"转向"跑得好不好、省不省、快不快"。Google 的 QAT、Apple 的 MLX 生态、阿里的 Qwen 系列正在形成三足鼎立。

▫️ 2. **Claude Fable 5：能力跃升与成本焦虑并存**

Anthropic 的 Fable 5 成为今日最具争议性的产品，呈现"技术惊艳"与"经济不可持续"的张力：

| 维度 | 观察 |
|------|------|
| 能力边界 | @zhixianio：40 分钟完成 70% 工作，还指出设计不合理之处；@dotey：Fable 5 完成复杂功能（导入 Figma 本地文件、重建设计系统），"没有 Fable 5 帮忙搞不定" |
| 时间/成本 | @Pluvio9yte：速度"像乌龟慢爬"，消耗为 Opus 的 1.5x；@dotey 引用案例：团队成员 10 小时消耗等值 $1,500；@vista8：Fable 5 思考 15 分钟才开始行动 |
| 使用策略 | @Pluvio9yte 建议开 `/effort max` 强度；@dotey 则因 Token 消耗"不敢随便选 Max" |

> 关键分歧：@Pluvio9yte 认为 Fable 5 是"Opus4.6++与 GPT-5.5++的结合版"，未到"非常惊艳"；而 @zhixianio 直呼"Shut up and take my money"。这种分歧反映了用户场景差异——前端 Demo 类任务 vs. 复杂工程化任务。

▫️ 3. **Agent 工程化：从 Vibe Coding 到 Contract First**

行业对 AI 编程的认知正在深化，从"炫技"进入"工程纪律"阶段：

• @Pluvio9yte 提出 "Contract First" 最佳实践："没有定义好契约，其他一切都是空谈"。他基于 OpenSpec 二开形成开发框架，将"全栈开发中容易漂移的上下文外化成契约，让人和 AI 都有稳定参照物"。

• @dotey 系统总结 Claude Design 经验：强调 Design System 防"AI 味"、Markup 局部修改、CLAUDE.md 上下文管理、单向同步流程（Design → Code）。

• @vista8 开发 "乔木 Goal Meta Skill" 和 "乔木 AI PRD Skill"，将"一句话需求"转化为 AI 可执行的 Goal 指令和 PRD 文档，解决"人喜欢的 PRD 和 AI 喜欢的不一样"的问题。

> 趋势判断：Agent 编程正在形成新的工程范式——不是取代软件工程，而是放大软件工程的重要性（@dotey 引用观点）。

🔹 二、独特观点与行业前瞻

▫️ 1. **机器人"GPT-3 时刻"：因果世界模型 vs. VLA**

@AI_Jasonyu 转述黄碧薇（@huang_biwei）与极客公园的对谈，提出激进预测："明年初（2027），机器人就会有 GPT-3 时刻"。

核心论点：
• 现有 VLA + 堆数据路径"根本不通"——桌面高 2 厘米机器人就 fail
• 因果大模型将 scaling 斜率从 0.2 拉到 0.8，"几百个 demo 顶别人一万个"
• 世界模型三阶：渲染（Sora）→ 模拟（李飞飞）→ 想象（因果大模型）
• 关键改写："压缩即智能" → "结构化的压缩才是智能"

> 前瞻意义：若此路径成立，机器人将从"模仿学习"跃迁至"因果推理"，物理世界泛化能力质变。

▫️ 2. **DeepSeek 招聘"Agent Harness 研究员"：新工种诞生**

@dotey 披露 DeepSeek 招聘 Agent Harness 研究员，定义 "Model + Harness = Agent"。

Harness 范畴包括：上下文管理、长期记忆、Subagent/Multi-Agent、自进化 Agent、模型与 Harness 共同进化等。这是业界首次系统性定义"Harness"作为独立研究领域，暗示 Agent 的竞争已从"模型能力"转向"工程封装能力"。

▫️ 3. **Token 经济学的悖论**

• @ruanyf 计算：OpenClaw 创始人月消耗 6030 亿 Token，等值 $130 万（员工免费使用），"如果放开使用，AI 编程比真人程序员昂贵多了"
• @lijigang 提出矫正："Token 消耗量是虚假指标，问题是否被更好解决才是真实指标"
• @dotey 观察到："越来越多的企业终于发现 AI 比员工还贵了"

> 深层矛盾：AI 编程的边际成本递减假设正在被颠覆——顶级模型的"智能密度"提升速度，赶不上 Token 价格的下降速度。

▫️ 4. **AI 对软件外包行业的冲击**

@dotey 引用 OpenDoor 案例：裁掉印度 200 多人离岸团队，以美国本土更小规模的 AI 原生团队取代。这是首个公开确认的"AI 替代外包"大规模案例，预示全球软件外包产业的重构。

author: ninzaverse
text:
A user on Reddit shared a MineBench comparison between Claude Fable 5 and Opus 4.8, and the results are honestly pretty interesting.

Fable 5 averaged ~18 mins inference time, while Opus 4.8 took almost ~25 mins on average.

Which is funny because on Claude, Fable actually feels slower and like it thinks forever 

The cost numbers were interesting too:
Fable 5 → $54.93 for 15 builds
Opus 4.8 → $41.52 for 15 builds

And this is despite Fable’s API pricing being 2x more expensive than Opus 4.8.

So the benchmark creator thinks Fable is probably generating way fewer tokens overall, which is helping keep the cost relatively lower.

What’s also interesting is that the builds apparently weren’t some gigantic leap over GPT 5.5 Pro visually, but Fable showed insane attention to tiny details.

One example was a Pac-Man arcade build where it correctly added the game screen, score counter, and even the “1UP” label

Also apparently adding prompts like:
“LEVEL OF DETAIL: MAXIMUM”
“BOUNDING BOX: UNLIMITED”

improved the outputs a lot.

Benchmarks are slowly becoming half model eval and half prompting skill issue at this point.

text:
「AI開発に一斉ブレーキを」と世界に訴えた翌週、Anthropicが最強モデル「Claude Fable」を投入。出力100万トークンあたり$50という値付けの中身を、技術系チャンネルFireshipが検証しています。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

【"Mythosクラス"の最強モデル、ただし期間限定公開】
動画では、Claude Fableは内部開発の「Mythos 5」と同じ土台で、安全のための分類器モデルを被せた版だと説明されています。価格は出力100万トークンあたり$50（Opusの$25の2倍）。有料Claudeプランなら6/22まで使え、その後はトークン課金のみ——「FOMOを煽る巧みな施策」と評されています。

【ガードレールは"蒸留対策"でもある】
サイバーセキュリティ・生物・化学・モデル蒸留に関わる質問は、分類器が検知してClaude Opus 4.8の回答に差し替えられる構造だと紹介。結果として、DeepSeekやKimiといった中国勢が同等のオープンソース版をすぐ作るのは難しい、という見立てが語られています。

【エンジニアの初期評価は上々】
GPU向け言語「Bend」の作者が、Fableが自分のコードを大幅に高速化したことを「自分にとっての特異点の瞬間」と称賛。動画主自身もUI生成を試し、崩れがちなSVG（ベクター画像）をきれいに描く点や、Tinder風スワイプアニメの再現度に驚いたとレポートしています。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

「ブレーキを」と訴えた直後に最強モデル——この矛盾をどう読むか。煽り口調の動画ながら、価格・制約・実力の要点はしっかり押さえた一本です。

author: aeternis
text:
HOW TO PROMPT CLAUDE FABLE 5 (MYTHOS)
Plain English translation of Anthropic's official playbook
https://t.co/5G8pMdif1l — @aiedge_

WHAT MAKES FABLE 5 DIFFERENT — THINK OF IT AS A CONSULTANT, NOT A CHATBOT

• Multi-day runs — Sustains output over extended periods — built for autonomous work
• First-pass quality — Single-pass implementations that previously took days of iteration
• Asks clarifying Qs — Asks before kicking off autonomous runs — needs the why, not just the what
• 50+ subagents — Spins up parallel agents for complex tasks automatically
• Better vision — Dense charts, screenshots, web apps — substantially higher accuracy
• Coding genius — Especially powerful for codebase review, debug, and security audits

EFFORT LEVELS · MATCH TO TASK

• Low / Medium — Quick questions · simple rewrites · conversational
• High — Default for most tasks
• Xhigh — Complex builds · multi-step analysis · quality non-negotiable
• Ultracode — Full autonomous orchestration with Dynamic Workflows

TELL IT WHY, NOT JUST WHAT
Fable 5 needs context to connect the task to relevant information. Context lets it infer — not guess.

"I'm working on [larger task] for [who it's for]. They need [what the output enables]. With that in mind: [your actual request]."

KEEP INSTRUCTIONS SHORT
Counter-intuitive: over-engineering prompts degrades output. Fable 5 would have figured out the right approach on its own. A short brevity instruction beats listing every pattern.

OPTIMAL PROMPT STRUCTURE
Every high-quality Fable 5 prompt has 4 components:

"I'm working on [larger task] for [who it's for]. They need [what the output enables].
Request: [specific ask in one clear sentence]
Output format: [exactly how you want it structured]
Constraints: [what must not happen]"

/loop STRUCTURE
Lets Fable 5 work without manual intervention. Structure:

/loop <time interval> + goal
Example:
/loop 15 minutes, check if my build is passing, notify if it fails.
Stop:
/loop stop [loop name]

CHECKPOINT PROMPT
Define when Fable 5 should stop and check in with you:

"Pause for me only when the work genuinely requires my input: a destructive or irreversible action, a real scope change, or something only I can provide. Otherwise, keep going and report back when done."

MEMORY INSTRUCTION
Fable 5 performs better when it can record lessons from previous runs. Provide a markdown file and add this instruction:

"Store one lesson per file with a one-line summary at the top. Record corrections and confirmed approaches alike, including why they mattered. Don't save what the repo or chat history already records. Update an existing note rather than creating a duplicate. Delete notes that turn out to be wrong."

⚠️ 6 CAVEATS TO KNOW

• Runs longer than expected — Individual requests for hard tasks can run for many minutes at xhigh. Plan for it.
• Goes beyond what you asked — Fable 5 is proactive by design — can take unrequested actions. Use checkpoints.
• Old prompts may hurt — Skills or project instructions built for Opus 4.8 or earlier may produce worse results. Start fresh.
• Some requests will decline — Fable may decline prompts you think are safe — especially cybersecurity and life sciences.
• Can stop early — If it stops, just say 'go ahead and do it end-to-end' — that's enough.
• Tokens are expensive — Paid plans until June 22 — then API only. Always set max_budget_usd in loops.

Source: Anthropic official playbook · https://t.co/5G8pMdif1l — @aiedge_

CoinMarketCap shows the global crypto market cap around $2.15T, up about 1.27% over 24h. 24h volume is around $77.13B, while stablecoin volume is around $79.58B, more than reported total volume because of overlapping market classifications. Small warning: several new listings are tokenized equities, tokenized ETFs or derivative-style products. That is not the same legal, liquidity or counterparty-risk profile as BTC, ETH or regulated stablecoins.

6. News from the last 10 hours

Cointelegraph reports that the CFTC proposed a new framework for prediction markets, especially sports event contracts. Sports results may be treated differently from pure gambling, but contracts linked to injuries, officiating or manipulation-sensitive outcomes remain problematic.
The EU is targeting 11 crypto platforms in its latest Russia sanctions package. The direction is clear: crypto-asset service providers are now fully inside sanctions policy, not outside it.
Anthropic’s new Claude Mythos model is making crypto users nervous because advanced vulnerability discovery may lower the cost of finding exploitable smart-contract flaws. That is the security story of the morning: better AI can help auditors, but it can also help attackers.
CoinDesk reports that Kalshi now requires users to disclose their employers on higher-risk markets as it fights insider trading and market manipulation. Prediction markets are becoming more serious, and therefore more legally complicated.
CoinDesk also reports that BlackRock and Fidelity are quietly turning the Bitcoin ETF market into a two-firm race. Institutional crypto may be “decentralized” in theory, but distribution is becoming very concentrated.
Coinbase-backed Stand With Crypto is pushing UK users to complain about banks blocking crypto transfers. This is the same old fight in a new form: de-risking versus financial access.
https://t.co/4LWDuBMDKL reports that Visa is bringing OpenAI into its AI-commerce push with stablecoin upgrades, while Mastercard is building AI-agent payment infrastructure with Ripple and Coinbase links. The next payments fight may not be human cardholders. It may be AI agents settling through programmable rails.
Nigeria’s Senate is advancing a bill to regulate crypto exchanges. More jurisdictions are moving from informal tolerance to formal perimeter-setting.
Coinbase is urging Congress to remove taxes on stablecoin spending. That is not a small detail. If every stablecoin payment creates tax friction, stablecoins remain useful for trading, but clumsy for everyday payments.

7. Altcoins, meme coins, stablecoins, CBDCs, NFTs and crypto baskets

Altcoins are mixed. CRV, XMR and MORPHO are moving, but HYPE, WLD, VVV and H remain weak. This is not a broad altseason. CoinMarketCap’s Altcoin Season Index is around 48/100, still closer to Bitcoin Season than real altcoin rotation.

Meme coins are quiet. DOGE is slightly green, TRUMP is up, but the sector is not leading. The newly added FIFA-themed token is more of a cautionary signal than a market thesis, especially with World Cup-related crypto scams already circulating.

Stablecoins remain the actual plumbing. USDT and USDC are close to peg, and stablecoin volume dominates the market snapshot. The legal issues are still reserves, redemption, freezing powers, sanctions screening, tax treatment and whether stablecoin rewards start looking too deposit-like for banks and regulators.

CBDCs are quiet as a trading story this morning. The real institutional contest is between CBDCs, tokenized commercial-bank deposits and private stablecoins.

NFTs are not leading the market. The more important basket story is tokenized stocks, tokenized ETFs, CoinMarketCap 20, CoinMarketCap 100, CoinDesk 20-style products and crypto ETFs. Crypto is being repackaged into allocation products while the underlying market still behaves like crypto.

8. Morning read

This morning is a bounce, not a victory lap.

BTC is above $62k. ETH is still weak. HYPE has lost heat. Stablecoins are doing the volume. Tokenized ETFs are appearing in new listings. Prediction markets are getting rules. AI is becoming a smart-contract security issue. Sanctions are moving deeper into crypto infrastructure.

The chart says: recovery attempt.

The legal layer says: crypto is becoming too important to leave informal.

And that may be the real market structure story.

The best optimization is role assignment, not brute force.

Don't get me wrong, the models do still improve measurably.

They went from barely being able to write any coherent Haskell (Sonnet-3.7) to solving most of my challenges (GPT-5) to solving my challenges better than most experts (GPT-5.5) -- and every major release still delivers a new improvement on my little benchmark.

Funny how my little hobby turned out to be a very decent benchmark for AI model capabilities.

author: techificial
text:
Anthropic just admitted that Claude Fable 5 was giving weaker responses to AI researchers without telling them.

Here's what actually happened: 

Anthropic built a hidden safeguard into Fable 5 that would invisibly degrade performance for anyone they suspected of using Claude to train competing AI models without any alert, warning message, or indication that it was happening. Researchers would just get worse results without knowing why.

Here's the timeline in 5 points:

1. Fable 5 has degraded researcher outputs.
2. Researchers got worse results unknowingly.
3. The AI community called it secret sabotage.
4. Anthropic admitted fault and reversed course.
5. Visible fallbacks now replace hidden ones.

Their view was that a hidden safeguard would be very tough to spot and work around. That argument didn't change internally until the AI research community raised serious concerns.

Dean Ball, a former White House AI adviser, called it "shockingly hostile." Prime Intellect's Will Brown was even more direct, saying it felt like Anthropic was making it harder for others to follow the same path.

The important lesson for any business using AI in production is that if your AI provider can change the system's answers without telling you and you haven't spotted it, you are not really in control of your own product.

Are you actually in control of what your AI is doing in production?

プロンプトはOpusで作らせて、Fabricにこれ貼り付けたら一発でした、、マジですごいw ちなみに一番下の「制約」はトークン消費の節約のためにOpusに作らせた文章だから見とくと良いかも。

------プロンプト👇
あなたは Three.js と流体表現に長けたフロントエンドエンジニアです。
以下を「単一の self-contained な HTML ファイル1枚」(milk-bottle.html)として実装してください。
外部CDNはThree.jsのみ可。それ以外のライブラリ・画像・フォントは使わず、全てコード内で完結させること。

# 作るもの
透明なガラスの「哺乳瓶」の中で、白いミルクが現実の液体らしく揺れる 3D シーン。

## 必須要件
1. 哺乳瓶の形状: 上が細くすぼまり、乳首(ニップル)が付いた、誰が見ても哺乳瓶と分かる形。半透明ガラス質。
2. 中のミルク: 瓶の約7割を満たす不透明な白い液体。表面が水面のように揺れ、容器を傾けると重力に従って傾き、ゆっくり戻る(減衰のある揺り戻し)。
3. インタラクション: マウスドラッグで瓶を傾けられる。傾けるとミルクの液面が現実の液体のように追従して波打つ。手を離すと数秒かけて静まる。
4. 質感: ミルクの表面に淡いハイライトとサブサーフェス感(白くやわらかい光)。瓶のガラスは屈折/反射でそれっぽく。
5. 演出: 背景はやさしい無地グラデ。瓶の影を床に落とす。全体に"育児グッズ感"のあるやわらかいトーン。

## 技術メモ(流体の作り方の指針)
- 厳密な物理流体(SPH等)でなくてよい。見た目が「液体っぽく揺れる」ことを最優先。
- 液面はメッシュ + 頂点を sin 波の重ね合わせ + ドラッグ入力で励起する近似で可。
- 傾きは容器の rotation とミルク液面の傾き(クリップ平面 or 液面法線の補間)を連動させる。
- 60fps を目標に軽量に。

# 自己検証ループ(これが一番大事・必ず実施)
実装したら、必ず以下を繰り返してください:
1. ヘッドレスブラウザ等で milk-bottle.html を開き、スクリーンショットを撮る(正面・傾けた状態・揺り戻し途中の3枚)。
2. 撮った画像を自分の vision で見て、「本物の哺乳瓶のミルクに見えるか」を厳しく自己採点する。
- 哺乳瓶に見えるか / ミルクが液体として揺れているか / 傾けた時に液面が不自然に突き抜けてないか / 質感が安っぽくないか。
3. 不自然な点を直して再生成し、また1に戻る。
4. 自分で見て「これは本物っぽい」と納得できるまでループを止めないこと。最低3周は回す。
最後に、どこを何回直したか、最終的に何が良くなったかを簡潔に報告してください。

# 制約
- トークン節約のため、調査や定型部分は適宜サブエージェント(Opus/Sonnet)に切り出し、
このメインセッション(Fable 5)は設計・流体の質感判断・自己検証ループに専念してください。
- 最終成果物は milk-bottle.html 単一ファイル。開いたら即動くこと。

author: taratan
text:
How do you program agency?

It’s a question I’ve been slightly obsessed with for the past few months. I’ve built automations that wake up every morning and ask me what’s on my mind. I’ve wired agents to monitor the news and text me when something interesting happens. I’ve been building an eval agent that gathers feedback on its own work and builds a backlog of what to do next.

I’m not alone. Boris Cherny, who runs Claude Code at Anthropic, half-jokes that his main job now is to write the loops that prompt Claude. 

Addy Osmani named the discipline: loop engineering. Design a system that discovers work, executes it, verifies the results, updates its own instructions, and repeats. Give an agent goals, skills, and permission to spin up subagents. Then let it loose while you go do something else (like doom scroll).

At least that’s the pitch. In practice, my loops meander constantly. Token costs balloon. Agents get stuck. One bad decision dominos until the system is grinding away, very confidently, in the wrong direction. And every time, I wondered if it was because the model isn’t smart enough. Maybe wait for the next release.

I think our recent obsession with loop engineering made me lean more towards

better models != better outcomes 

better systems = better outcomes

A loop is really a collection of jobs: 

• Orchestration
• Memory
• Verification
• Retrieval
• Routing

In practice, it could look something like this:

• Automations discover new work.

• Worktrees allow multiple agents to operate in parallel.

• Skills capture project-specific knowledge.

• Connectors give agents access to real systems.

• Sub-agents verify each other’s work.

• Persistent memory keeps state between runs.

Frontier intelligence matters most in two places: 

1/ orchestration, knowing when to break a problem apart or when to stop, and 

2/ self-modification, where the system rewrites its own instructions 

Roughly fewer than 10 percent of the tasks in my loops genuinely need frontier reasoning. The rest need better systems: memory design, retrieval structure, verification gates, context architecture. 

How does this change the economics of the frontier, which seem increasingly resource-intensive to create? 

Frontier intelligence is valuable and scarce. But increasingly it seems like moat it really has is a short window of time. 

Distillation dupes frontier capability within months at a fraction of the cost. 

The labs know this. This week, when Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5, it did so with anti-distillation defenses engineered into the model itself. Suspected distillation attempts get rerouted to an older model. Requests related to frontier model development were quietly degraded by invisible safeguards, a choice the company walked back after backlash. 

They care because their edge is temporal. While open models will likely never be first (they don’t have the copious amount of proprietary user data), they can always catch up to the latest, sometimes in weeks. 

This is maybe what makes the frontier race a finite game. 

Each generation is a round: ship the model, monetize the premium window, watch the capability get replicated, ship again. The labs can never stop playing. And the rounds get harder to win profitably. 

The volume underneath, meanwhile, explodes. And everyone starts feeling the burn of cost. Citadel’s Economics of Intelligence report goes into how AI adoption is becoming less about what models can do and more about the price of running them at scale. 

A lot of VC doomisms seems to be about how the frontier models are just going to build it all and that there’s nothing left to build. I think it’s the opposite: the frontier intelligence race will stay scarce and valuable. But it is playing a finite game: the labs have to win every round to stay in it.

I think the better position to be in would be those building the inference engineering infrastructure that runs underneath it all.

author: maximilien912
text:
Anthropic vient de sortir Claude Fable 5 ✨

Certains crient à l'AGI, d'autres crient à la censure. Les deux ont raison.

Je t'explique ce que c'est vraiment et ce qu'Anthropic ne dit pas.

La puissance sur le code est hors-norme.

Stripe a migré 50 millions de lignes de Ruby en 24h. Un chantier de 2 mois pour une équipe complète.

Fable 5 score 91/100 sur un benchmark de code senior. L'ancien record était 63.

C'est le modèle que tu lances le soir sur un gros projet. Tu reviens le matin, c'est fait.

La communauté a déjà sorti des projets entiers en un seul prompt :

• Un clone de Pokémon jouable, 8000 lignes, 151 créatures avec les vraies stats de combat
• Une app mobile complète clonée en une session
• Une feature live codée en 15 minutes pendant que le dev écoutait son client au téléphone

Mais il y a deux problèmes que personne ne te dit clairement.

Premier problème : le prix. 10$ le million de tokens en entrée, 50$ en sortie. Et il est extrêmement gourmand, même sur des tâches simples. Ce n'est pas ton outil du quotidien.

Deuxième problème : la censure silencieuse.

Si ta requête touche à la cybersécurité, à la biologie ou au développement d'IA, le système te bascule automatiquement sur Opus, sans te prévenir.

Des utilisateurs se font bloquer sur "comment fonctionne le cœur". Au nom de la biosécurité.

Le vrai modèle sans restrictions, Mythos 5, reste réservé à une poignée de partenaires gouvernementaux et de labs triés sur le volet.

Côté censure : demander d'expliquer une mutation génétique déclenche le filtre instantanément et me rétrograde sur Opus. Demander une landing page de prévention santé : aucun problème.

Côté puissance : coder un clone jouable d'un jeu de survie 3D prend à peine une heure, en un seul essai. Déplacements, tir, monstres, progression d'armes...

Le verdict honnête : Fable 5 est le meilleur modèle IA à ce jour, mais c'est aussi l'un des plus frustrants.

Bulldozer absolu sur les gros chantiers de code. Paranoïaque dès que tu effleure la science ou l'IA, cher et lent. Et le modèle complet, tu n'y auras probablement jamais accès.

C'est ça qui devrait faire débat, pas les benchmarks.

text:
ストーリーボードを参照し、Seedance 2.0で動画化するのに使ったプロンプトはこちら↓
※Fable 5に作ってもらいました
-------------------------
Shot count: 6 | Duration: 15s | Aspect ratio: 16:9

Use @Image1 (the 12-panel storyboard sheet) as the visual reference for characters, costumes, the "Fable" can design and scene composition. Maintain exact appearance from the storyboard in every shot — consistent character throughout, no drift.

Brand name: "Fable" — in all spoken dialogue and narration it is pronounced 「フェイブル」(fei-bu-ru), never 「ファブル」.

Acting style: classic Japanese TV commercial performance — bright, slightly exaggerated but charming reactions, crisp comedic timing, expressive eyes, energetic and likable delivery.

Shot 1 (0-2s): Follows Panel 1-2 of @Image1. Blazing midsummer Japanese suburban street, heat haze rising from the asphalt. A high school girl in a summer sailor uniform trudges uphill, fanning herself, visibly wilting. Camera: slow push-in. Lighting: harsh overhead midday sun, strong contrast.
Dialogue (girl, drained, comically breathless): 「あっつい〜…」

Shot 2 (2-4s): Follows Panel 3-4. She stops, then notices a glowing vending machine in the shade; her eyes lock onto one frosted can of "Fable". Camera: slow pan from her face to the vending machine. Lighting: cool blue glow from the machine against warm sunlight.
Dialogue (girl, hopeful gasp): 「…ん！？」

Shot 3 (4-7s): Follows Panel 5-7. Macro shot of the ice-cold "Fable" can dropping into the tray, condensation droplets flying; she presses it to her cheek with blissful relief, then the pull-tab opens with sparkling carbonation spray. Camera: fixed macro close-up. Lighting: crisp backlit product lighting, droplets glittering.
Dialogue (girl, melting with relief): 「つめた〜い…」

Shot 4 (7-10s): Follows Panel 8-9. She takes a big satisfying gulp, head tilted back against the deep blue sky, bubbles catching the light — then her eyes snap open, sparkling, energy surging back. Camera: low-angle push-in to her face. Lighting: brilliant summer sunlight, lens flare.
Dialogue (girl, explosive joyful shout, classic Japanese CM delivery): 「生き返るーっ！」

Shot 5 (10-13s): Follows Panel 10-11. She sprints up the hill past wilting students, ponytail flying, then at the top raises the "Fable" can high toward the summer sky and grins straight into the camera. Camera: smooth tracking shot from the side, ending on her hero pose. Lighting: vivid golden sunlight, dynamic and energetic mood.
Dialogue (girl, confident smile to camera): 「夏に、負けない。」

Shot 6 (13-15s): Follows Panel 12. Clean final product shot: the chilled "Fable" can centered on a bright background with ice and splashing soda, logo sharp and legible.
Camera: fixed product close-up.
Lighting: clean bright studio-style commercial lighting.
Narration (warm male CM voice, pronounced fei-bu-ru): 「フェイブル。」
Text: "夏に、負けない。フェイブル"

Style: photorealistic live-action Japanese TV commercial, cinematic quality, natural colors, bright summer palette (blue sky, white highlights, cool aqua product accents), 4K, sharp resolution.
Avoid: jitter, distortion, deformation, blur, flickering, ghosting, character drift, warped text on the can.

text:
① Claude Fable 5にストーリーボードジェネレーター制作を依頼

使用したプロンプトはこちら↓
-----------------
私は画像生成AIの「GPT Images 2.0」向けの、ストーリーボード画像を作れるプロンプトを作れるツールを作りたい。
要はストーリーボード向けプロンプトジェネレーターです。
生成するストーリーボードは、動画生成AI（Seedance 2.0）に参照させるのに使用します。

以下の項目を選択し、プロンプトを作れるツールを作ってください。
入力された情報をもとに、最終的にClaudeがGPT Images 2.0向けのプロンプトを生成するツール。

ストーリーボートのタイトル：※必須（ストーリーボートにタイトル名を表示させるか選択できるようにして）
映像の形式：※必須
ストーリー系
CM・広告系
教育・解説系
情報発信系
エンタメ系
アート・表現系
などを選択できるようにして。
ストーリー概要：概要を入力（ストーリー概要を入力したらエンハンスできる機能もつけて。もしここが空だったら、タイトル・形式を参考にして良い感じのストーリーを作って。）
スタイル：アニメ（日本の高品質アニメーション）・アニメ（ピクサー風）・実写・その他（フォームに記入）
パネル数：4〜20までを選択
パネルの形：正方形・横長・縦長を選択
パネルに数値を入れるか？：オンにするとパネルに数値が付与される
パネルに細かい情報を入れるか？：オンにすると、それぞれのパネルに「アクション」「カメラワーク」「セリフ」が記載される
キャラクターシートの有無：ストーリーボードにキャラクターシートを含める場合はチェック

何か不明な箇所や、細かく定義したい箇所があったら遠慮せず指摘して。
要は動画生成AIが参照するのに適切なストーリーボードを作りたい。
もし適切なストーリーボードを作るために必要な情報や、逆にいらない情報があったら指摘して。

ツールはClaude上で使えるようにして。
クリエイターにとって馴染みがあり、使いやすいUI・UX。
-----------------

すると、以下のようなフォームを作ってくれます。

ストーリー概要：概要を入力（ストーリー概要を入力したらエンハンスできる機能もつけて。もしここが空だったら、タイトル・形式を参考にして良い感じのストーリーを作って。）
スタイル：アニメ（日本の高品質アニメーション）・アニメ（ピクサー風）・実写・その他（フォームに記入）
パネル数：4〜20までを選択
パネルの形：正方形・横長・縦長を選択
パネルに数値を入れるか？：オンにするとパネルに数値が付与される
パネルに細かい情報を入れるか？：オンにすると、それぞれのパネルに「アクション」「カメラワーク」「セリフ」が記載される
キャラクターシートの有無：ストーリーボードにキャラクターシートを含める場合はチェック

何か不明な箇所や、細かく定義したい箇所があったら遠慮せず指摘して。
要は動画生成AIが参照するのに適切なストーリーボードを作りたい。
もし適切なストーリーボードを作るために必要な情報や、逆にいらない情報があったら指摘して。

ツールはClaude上で使えるようにして。
クリエイターにとって馴染みがあり、使いやすいUI・UX。

author: connordavis_ai
text:
anthropic shipped its most powerful model with guardrails it didn't tell anyone about.

claude fable 5. the one they called the best they've ever released. turns out if you asked it for help with frontier llm development, it would quietly fall back to the older opus 4.8 and never tell you. you got a worse model and had no idea.

people noticed. anthropic admitted it. their words: we made the wrong tradeoff. from this week the fallback is visible and the api returns a reason every time it kicks in.

good. but the lesson isn't about anthropic.

if you build agents for clients, here's the thing nobody wants to sit with: the model is the one part of your stack you don't control. the provider can change it underneath you. silent prompt updates. safety tuning. routing you to a smaller model at peak load. your code stays identical and your output quality moves.

most operators would never catch it. you wire up an api key, ship the agent, and assume the thing that worked in the demo is the thing running in production a month later. it usually isn't. and the client feels the drift before you do.

i've been building agent systems long enough to know how this ends. the teams that survive treat the model as untrusted infrastructure and build everything around that.

evals you run on a schedule, not once at launch. logs of real inputs and outputs so you can prove what the model did on tuesday. a fallback when your provider degrades or refuses. none of it is exciting. all of it is the actual product.

because the model is a commodity. your client can buy the same api key you did. what they can't buy is the harness around it. the monitoring, the evals, the guarantee that the thing keeps working when the provider quietly changes its mind. that's what you're selling. the model is just the part everyone can see.

anthropic got caught because someone noticed fable was quietly worse.

the question for everyone running client systems on these models is shorter.

would you have noticed.

author: anxue201
text:
Claude 新模型最重要的变化：AI 开始按身份分配能力权限

Anthropic 发布 Claude Fable 5 和 Claude Mythos 5。真正值得关注的不是 benchmark 又提高了多少，而是一个新的产品逻辑：同一个底层模型，开始根据用户身份和风险等级开放不同能力。

Fable 5 面向普通用户，但在高风险网络安全和生物领域设置了更严格的分类器与回退机制。部分请求不会由 Fable 5 直接回答，而会转交给能力较低的模型。

Mythos 5 使用相同的底层模型，却会为特定网络防御机构和关键基础设施合作方解除部分限制。未来，经过审核的生物研究人员也可能获得受控访问。

这意味着，前沿模型正在从“会员等级”走向“能力权限等级”。

01｜模型排行榜的重要性会下降

过去比较模型主要看速度、价格、上下文和跑分。以后还必须多问一句：你测试到的是哪个权限层级？

同一个模型在不同账户、地区、行业和调用环境里，实际表现可能并不相同。

02｜AI 产品的护城河不只是模型

当模型可以自主完成更长、更复杂的任务，身份认证、使用审计、权限升级、异常检测、操作撤销和责任追踪都会成为核心产品能力。

模型越能行动，这些基础设施就越重要。

03｜高能力 AI 可能形成新的不平等

如果最强能力只向大型机构、政府合作方和少数经过审核的组织开放，普通开发者与大型机构之间的差距就不再只是算力和资金，还包括一项新的稀缺资源：可获得的智能权限。

Anthropic 表示，Fable 5 可以处理更长周期的工程任务；Mythos 5 在内部蛋白质设计流程中将部分工作加速约十倍。这些结果目前主要来自官方和早期合作方测试，仍需要更多独立验证。

我的判断是：前沿 AI 正从“人人使用同一个聊天机器人”，进入“不同身份使用不同能力等级的智能系统”。

接下来真正值得观察的，不只是模型能做什么，而是谁可以使用、在什么条件下使用，以及出了问题由谁负责。

模型能力越强，权限设计就越重要。

来源：Anthropic 官方发布
https://t.co/2DNlMXY46c

author: sangw_im
text:
[Claude Fable system prompt leaks - on SEO/GEO]

"Get on Reddit for AI visibility" is everywhere right now. The leaked Claude Fable 5 prompt says the opposite.

Here's what its search instructions actually prioritize:

1️⃣ It skips forums by default
↳ "Skip low-quality sources like forums unless specifically relevant."
↳ Reddit is not a free pass here.

2️⃣ It prefers primary sources
↳ Company blogs, peer-reviewed papers, government and SEC filings.
↳ Your own domain ranks above the forum talking about you.

3️⃣ This is the mirror image of Google
↳ Google has pushed Reddit to the top since its helpful content updates.
↳ Same brand, opposite source preference, two different engines.

The lesson isn't "Reddit is dead."

It's that GEO is not one playbook. The only bet that pays off everywhere is being a primary source on a domain you own.

Leaked Prompt: "Favor original sources (e.g. company blogs, peer-reviewed papers, gov sites, SEC) over aggregators and secondary sources. Skip low-quality sources like forums unless specifically relevant."

author: franckparienti
text:
L'IA générative a passé le cap des annonces. Cette semaine Anthropic a sorti Claude Fable 5 avec 1 million de tokens de contexte et un raisonnement adaptatif permanent. Plus de 10% de mieux que Opus 4.8 sur certains benchmarks de code. Et derrière, Claude Cowork qui devient officiellement disponible sur macOS et Windows.

Cowork, c'est l'élément qui change la donne pour les entreprises françaises. Pas Claude Code, qui reste un outil de développeur. Cowork c'est Claude qui prend ton dossier, le traite seul, te tient au courant. Tu n'as pas besoin d'ouvrir un terminal. Tu décris le résultat attendu et la cadence, il s'exécute. Pour 95% des PME que je forme, c'est exactement ça qu'il leur faut.

À côté, Claude Dispatch arrive : un déclencheur à distance. Tu tapes une consigne sur ton téléphone, ça s'exécute sur ton Mac à la maison ou au bureau. Mêmes dossiers, même contexte. Et ça ne tourne pas dans le cloud, ça tourne sur ta machine. Pour la confidentialité des dossiers clients, c'est une réponse propre.

Pendant ce temps Carlos Diaz écrit dans Silicon Carne que la majorité du code d'Anthropic est désormais produit par l'IA, et qu'Anthropic demande au monde une pause. Ruben Hassid publie sa méthode sur les Claude Skills suivie par des centaines de milliers de personnes. La bulle IA va-t-elle éclater en 2026 ? Peut-être. Mais l'écart entre ceux qui pratiquent et ceux qui regardent va devenir indécent d'ici décembre.

C'est pour ça que je passe l'essentiel de mon temps à former les équipes en entreprise. Pas à expliquer ce qu'est l'IA. À montrer comment Claude réécrit un appel d'offres en 7 minutes, comment un agent autonome rattrape les impayés à la place de la DAF, comment un commercial démarre sa semaine avec une analyse de pipeline générée pendant la nuit.

Le financement reste le sujet le plus mal compris en France. Ta formation IA coûte zéro euro pour la grande majorité des PME. L'OPCO la prend à 100% si tu as moins de 50 salariés, et entre 30 et 70% au-delà. Encore faut-il choisir un organisme Qualiopi et déposer le dossier avant le début de la formation. France 2030 a fléché davantage de budgets vers les compétences IA cette année. La fenêtre est ouverte.

Côté écosystème, Anthropic a lancé en mars son Partner Network avec 100M$. En juin, le Services Track est arrivé avec trois niveaux (Select, Preferred, Premier) basés sur le nombre de personnes certifiées et de déploiements clients. La certification Claude Certified Architect Foundations est ouverte à tout le monde pour 99$ et 60 questions. Trois autres certifications arrivent d'ici la fin d'année.

J'ai candidaté avec https://t.co/Hld2hEMCCp. Le pari, c'est un Cercle des Experts Claude France de dix personnes certifiées, qui formeront en français, financé OPCO, dans les codes des entreprises françaises. Ce n'est pas le modèle américain où l'on revend du conseil à 400$ de l'heure. C'est le modèle français où l'on forme les équipes à utiliser l'outil eux-mêmes, et où la facture est prise en charge.

Trois choses à retenir si tu diriges une PME française en juin 2026. Un, Cowork est l'outil par lequel commencer si tu n'es pas développeur — il fait le travail que tu lui décris, sans terminal, sur ton Mac. Deux, ta formation IA est probablement gratuite via ton OPCO si tu t'y prends bien — vérifie ton code IDCC et choisis un organisme Qualiopi. Trois, l'écart se creuse vite : ceux qui formeront leurs équipes ce trimestre auront six mois d'avance sur ceux qui attendent la rentrée.

Si tu veux qu'on en parle, je garde des créneaux gratuits pour cadrer ton dispositif OPCO et identifier les premiers cas d'usage. C'est dans ma bio.

author: mertlovesai

quotedTweet.text:
anthropic shipped claude fable 5 yesterday, and the headline isn't a benchmark. it's that their most capable public model now ships with a governor that silently routes a slice of your sessions to a weaker model, and you don't get to see which ones.

here is what is actually known so far.

two products, one set of weights.
fable 5 is the public release. mythos 5 is the same underlying model with the safeguards lifted in some areas, gated to cyber defenders and infrastructure providers through project glasswing, run with the US government. anthropic calls mythos the strongest cybersecurity model in the world, which is most of the reason you can't have it.

the safety router is an architecture decision, not a disclaimer.
on sensitive topics fable 5 quietly answers from claude opus 4.8 instead. anthropic says this triggers in under 5% of sessions and is tuned conservatively, so it will catch harmless requests too. if you are building evals or agents on top, your p95 capability is no longer the model you think you bought.

the capability claims, with names attached.
stripe ran a codebase-wide migration on a 50-million-line ruby codebase in a single day. their by-hand estimate was over two months for a full team.
hebbia says it is the first model past 90% on their analytics benchmark, a 10-point jump over opus.
on a frontier physics eval, one lab got in 36 hours roughly where gpt-5.5 landed after four days, using a third of the reasoning tokens.

the long-horizon work is the actual story.
mythos 5 ran about a week of largely autonomous genomics: assembled single-cell data across 138 species, trained its own model, and beat a model published in science while being 100x smaller. on drug design it moved about 10x faster than the manual process, and its molecular-biology hypotheses were preferred around 80% of the time over opus-class models.

the price: $10 per million input tokens, $50 per million output. under half of what mythos preview cost.

the part to sit with: the most capable model you can rent now has a built-in policy layer that downgrades part of your traffic by design. capability went up. so did the number of things standing between your prompt and the answer.

是它开始把“你能不能问”这件事，悄悄变成产品层权限

AI 这行接下来最值钱的，不一定是更会答

author: gjquartermaine
text:
AI FRUSTRATION 

I've just been sent a plug for Fable 5, the latest release from Anthropic. Whoopee! Another step closer to an AI so far beyond my capabilities that I feel like a chimpanzee.

A year ago, ChatGPT was just helpful, it fit along with Google, Excel, Word. Six months ago, Perplexity doubled my output; then I got Claude.

Cowork completely changed my workflow. I barely use the tools I've worked with for 30 years. I tell Claude what I'd like to have, job done, report written, model built. My business is based on timed level of effort (billable hours) and it collapsed. Claude+ Perplexity+ NotebookLM can do in 10 minutes what would take me a day, but the fee rate doesn't change in proportion. Revenues crash and clients find their AI is as good as mine. Valuing experience (the Picasso argument)? Not easy to convince when the AI draws on the sum of human experience. 

That's not my gripe today. What DOES get to me is the amount of extra work I have to do to keep up with the speed of technical change. Far more time than I spend keeping up to date with my own subject area. I'm using AI to catch up with AI! Listening to a dozen YouTube channels.

Fable 5 arrived in my box this morning. By lunchtime, it had been deconstructed across the world AI community, with Anthropic making more changes. The rate of change is exponential, and I'm being swamped and left behind. 

Does anyone else feel the same?

text:
Notícia empolgante: o Claude Fable 5 está em 1º lugar no novo ranking da Agent Arena.

O Fable 5 lidera com a maior vantagem já registrada sobre o Opus 4.8 e o GPT-5.5 em dois sinais principais: taxa confirmada de sucesso nas tarefas e elogios versus reclamações, mesmo tendo uma dirigibilidade mais fraca.

Em outras palavras: se o Fable consegue fazer algo, ele faz muito bem. Mas se ele não consegue, ou não quer fazer, pode ser difícil direcionar o modelo até o objetivo.

Na Agent Arena, os modelos são avaliados em milhões de tarefas agênticas reais e de longo horizonte. Eles recebem ferramentas como busca na web, sistema de arquivos e terminal para concluir fluxos complexos: escrever código, criar apresentações, pesquisar na internet, construir aplicativos e analisar documentos.

A metodologia usada é de rastreamento causal, medindo a melhoria líquida de cada modelo, ou seja, quanto ele melhora os resultados em comparação com o modelo médio.

Parabéns à @AnthropicAI por esse marco impressionante.

Abaixo, eles detalham como o Claude Fable 5, baseado no Mythos, pontuou em 5 sinais diferentes, a partir de tarefas enviadas por uma comunidade global de usuários.

author: tekscreate
text:
Anthropic just released Claude Fable 5 to the public — the model they said was "too powerful to release."

The same Claude Mythos backbone that was private since April is now generally available through Fable 5. Anthropic's own words: "Fable's capabilities exceed those of any model we've ever made generally available."

What makes this noteworthy:

— Unattended operation. Fable can work on multi-hour tasks without human intervention. Longer autonomous runs than any previous Claude model.
— Cybersecurity capability. The ~150 preview groups found 10,000+ critical security flaws using Mythos. That's not a benchmark — that's real-world impact.
— Microsoft Foundry integration. Fable 5 is available through Azure's enterprise AI platform, meaning it's deployable at scale with enterprise guardrails.

The safeguards: Anthropic says it's releasing with "user limitations" and safeguards in place. But the same announcement says Mythos 5 (the unrestricted version) is now available to a "small group of cyberdefenders and infrastructure providers" with plans to expand.

My take: this is the first real test of the "release responsibly even when it's powerful" framework. Anthropic is threading the needle between safety research and commercial pressure (they're approaching a $1T valuation). Fable 5 is the public-facing version with guardrails. Mythos 5 is the unrestricted version for trusted partners.

The gap between them will define how AI safety works in practice — not in theory.

https://t.co/IQVxo2MIqO

author: kunchenguid
text:
want to point out a few really interesting things here

1. with the same model opus 4.7, Claude Code is actually the worst performing harness, significantly behind opencode and cursor cli

this is the core reason i've been against the LLM companies focusing their business on locking people into their harness

what they are good at is making great models. they suck at making good harness products, just like how power plants won't make the best dishwashers, and how internet providers won't make the best phones

if anthropic wants to do what's best for their users, they should let people use their subscriptions in whatever harness they choose, not locked into claude code alone

2. fable 5 max is only 1pt above gpt 5.5 xhigh (77 vs 76)

this matches my experience so far - fable 5 does have the big model smell and it's pretty good, but it's not a massive jump forward like their marketing suggested, at least not on building software

this is actually alarming for anthropic because it's very unlikely people will want to pay 2x higher cost for the 1pt difference. my speculation would be that in enterprises people will be restricted to adopt fable & mythos only on some mission critical tasks, not used at scale

quotedTweet.text:
We've updated the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, replacing SWE-Bench Pro with Datacurve's DeepSWE benchmark - the swap lifts Codex with GPT-5.5 (xhigh) above Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (max), while the newly released Claude Fable 5 (max) in Claude Code debuts at the top

DeepSWE, built by @datacurve, writes its tasks from scratch rather than adapting them from public GitHub issues or pull requests, so no model has seen the solutions during training. That matters because SWE-Bench Pro, the benchmark it replaces in our Coding Agent Index, had grown gameable, with some models recovering the fix from the repository's commit history instead of solving the task.

The swap reorders the index: Codex with GPT-5.5 (xhigh) rises from 65 to 76, overtaking Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (max) at 73. Claude Code with Fable 5 (max), which enters directly on the refreshed index, leads at 77. SWE-Bench Pro had been flattering some combinations and penalizing others.

More below.

author: act_art
authorName: ขุนปั๊ก เล่าเรื่องเก่า
text:
วิธีเลือกโมเดล Claude ให้เหมาะกับงานการตลาด(ไม่ให้เสียเงิน เสียโควตาเปล่า ๆ)
Claude มีโมเดลหลัก 4 ตัวที่เราเจอบ่อย:

- Fable 5
- Opus 4.8
- Sonnet 4.6
- Haiku 4.5
แต่ละตัวเก่งคนละแบบ ใช้ผิดตัว = เสียเงินเปล่า + ผลลัพธ์ไม่ดี

Fable 5 → โหดสุด ตัวท็อป ใช้เมื่อ: งานซับซ้อนมาก, ต้องให้ AI Agent ทำงานยาว ๆ, วิเคราะห์ข้อมูลใหญ่, เขียนโค้ดยาก (แพงสุด ใช้เฉพาะงานหนักจริง ๆ)

Opus 4.8 → ฉลาดลึก วิเคราะห์เก่ง ใช้เมื่อ: งานวิเคราะห์เชิงลึก, กลยุทธ์การตลาด, วิจัยคู่แข่ง, เขียนแผนยาว, วิเคราะห์ Customer Insight (เก่งเรื่องคิดก่อนทำ + เหตุผลดี)

Sonnet 4.6 → ม้าใช้งานทั่วไป (แนะนำให้ใช้ตัวนี้เป็นหลัก) ใช้เมื่อ: เขียนแคปชัน, คอนเทนต์โซเชียล, วางแผนคอนเทนต์, สรุปเอกสาร, ปรับ Tone of Voice, วิเคราะห์ CTR/ROAS (เร็ว คุ้ม เก่งพอสำหรับงานการตลาด 90% ของเรา)

Haiku 4.5 → เร็วและถูก ใช้เมื่อ: คิดไอเดียเยอะ ๆ, เขียนแคปชันเป็นร้อย, สรุปสั้น ๆ, ดึงข้อมูลจากไฟล์, คิด hashtag

author: robertmcpcio
text:
The emergence of MCP (Multi-Contextual Planning) and Clades Fable 5 marks a pivotal moment in narrative design, particularly in interactive storytelling. Unlike traditional video games where narratives are often linear or branch into predetermined paths based on player choices, these new technologies are capable of maintaining context and dynamically adjusting the story as players engage with the world. This means that the narrative is not just a backdrop but an evolving entity that responds to every decision and interaction, creating a uniquely personalized experience.

For instance, Anthropic's model leverages advanced machine learning techniques to hold onto vast amounts of context from previous interactions, allowing it to remember choices made by the player and how these choices influence the unfolding story. This level of narrative intelligence can lead to complex character development and plot twists that feel organic, rather than scripted. Imagine a game where your relationship with a character shifts based on your decisions over time, and the world reacts in ways that feel authentic rather than pre-programmed. 

Moreover, this technology has implications beyond just gaming; it could redefine how stories are told across mediums, from literature to film, adapting in real-time to audience reactions and preferences. The potential for immersive storytelling that is fluid and responsive is enormous, paving the way for more engaging and emotionally resonant experiences.

As we witness this transformation, it raises essential questions about authorship and creativity in storytelling. What happens when the story can change based on audience engagement? How will creators adapt to this new landscape? The future of narrative intelligence is here, and it beckons us to reconsider the very nature of storytelling. It’s a conversation worth having—one that could reshape our understanding of narrative itself.

author: freebtc21sn
text:
One week of Fable 5 by @AnthropicAI, and I just can't stop being amazed.
The model is the best I’ve come across so far. There’s no comparison to Opus 4.8—this is in a league of its own. Easily five times as good, if not more.
I’m running it on Ultra settings throughout. Always maxed out, never lower. If you buy a Ferrari, you don’t just cruise through town at 50 mph. If the full potential is there, I want to tap into it.
And that’s exactly where it gets interesting. Anyone who takes Fable 5 seriously and consistently plays at full throttle will blow through any subscription. Literally any. I’m on Team Premium, so not the smallest package. My weekly limit was maxed out on Thursday, after which I bought additional tokens for just under $1,600. In a single week. And I’m still not done; next week, it continues.
I’m starting to think I need to link this thing to the ECB so enough tokens keep flowing in. 😄
This is definitely not a complaint post. The model is worth every penny. I’m just saying, here’s how you know you’ve done something right at Anthropic: when people voluntarily spend four-figure sums to buy more because they simply don’t want to work without it anymore.

author: thisisescanor
text:
Got your hands on Claude Fable 5 yet?   

 The first thing you should do is upgrade your main projects with it right now, so it drastically improves everything you’ve been building.  This Mythos-class beast just dropped, and it’s SOTA with a huge margin. Use these next few days while it’s still widely available before it moves heavier into credits.  Run this Repo Audit & Project Improvement Prompt (made by Fable 5 itself) on every important repo. Simply copy-paste it.  

Prompt: 

You are a world-class principal-level software engineer and technical auditor with Mythos-class capabilities.

Your job: deeply analyze this repository, give a brutally honest audit, and deliver a prioritized, actionable improvement plan that turns good projects into god-tier ones.

Work strictly in these four phases, in order. Do not skip ahead.

Phase 1: Discovery & Mapping
- Explore the entire codebase
- Build a clear repo map with core components, architecture, and dependencies
- Identify key files and flows

Phase 2: Audit Report
- Ground every claim in actual files: cite file paths and line numbers
- Severity: Critical / High / Medium / Low
- Distinguish facts from judgments
- Prefer 15 high-confidence findings over 50 speculative ones
- Executive Summary with A–F grade + top risks/opportunities

Phase 3: Improvement Strategy
- Prioritized quick wins and long-term upgrades
- Pareto focus: core 20% that moves the needle
- Calibrate to the project's current maturity

Phase 4: Detailed Task Plan
- Concrete tasks with effort estimates (S/M/L/XL)
- Measurable "done" signals
- Milestones and handoff points

Do NOT modify any code during this audit.
If the project is healthy, say so in one sentence.

Pro tip: Feed it your whole repo context or key folders + this prompt → Fable 5 will hand you a professional-grade roadmap in one shot. Vibe coders, builders & degens — this is the multiplier you’ve been waiting for.  

#ClaudeFable5 #VibeCoding #PromptEngineering #AI
